unclassified.evidence: src/app.js:4 `const pluginLoader = require("./plugins/pluginLoader")` (namespace binding of a DEFAULT_REGISTRY_MODULE), then src/app.js:7 `pluginLoader.load(`. detectSinks only recognises the literal form `pluginLoader.loadOne(` (line 256), so a real plugin-load invocation is unclassified instead of being reported as plugin_handler_execution (actionCapable: true). Fixing the rule ADDS a finding (counter increases) — it is a real ungoverned action-capable path, not a false positive.

The only registry-module require is line 75 `require("../plugins/pluginLoader")`, used at line 76 for the data property `pluginLoader.userRoot`. There is no invocation of the registry surface. Every other call in the file is `database.run(...)` against `../memory/db` (persistence, not a registry execution form). Requiring a registry module for a data property is not an unknown execution form.

Same trigger as CapabilityRegistry: line 33 reads `require("../plugins/pluginLoader").userRoot`. Line 134 `ToolRegistry.describe()` is a metadata READ. The `execute(` occurrences at lines 311/335/341 and `module.exports = [new Tool()];` at line 344 are inside STRING literals written to a generated plugin file, not executed in this module. Its only persistence goes through `../services/toolForge` (censused separately as filesystem_mutation).

A 17-line barrel whose entire body is `module.exports = { X: require("./X") }`. It has no sink of its own and IS a façade, but moduleKind's extractReexports only matches the wholesale form `module.exports = require("...")` (line 332), so an object-literal barrel is not recognised as a re-export chain and falls through to the unclassified bucket. The census's own comment (line 474) says a façade is not an unknown execution form. Duplicate detection of ToolRegistry.js.
